items: The telegraph office closes at dusk, its single bulb flickering over keys that have been silent since morning.
Salt crusts the deck planks as the trawler rolls through fog somewhere off the Flemish coast.
In the planetarium's copper dome, dust motes spiral through projector light at three in the afternoon.
The quarry fills with amber light each dawn, illuminating limestone faces cut into geometric shelves.
Midnight finds the university library's rare book room locked, though a desk lamp still burns inside.
The refugee processing center opens its doors at eight, fluorescent lights humming over rows of plastic chairs.
Monsoon rain hammers the tin roof of the rural clinic where two examination tables wait empty.
The subway platform smells of brake dust and heating metal as the last train pulls away near midnight.
At the textile mill, looms clatter in the pre-dawn darkness while frost patterns the tall windows.
The observatory perches on the volcanic ridge, its white dome stark against the afternoon's gathering clouds.
In the courthouse basement, filing cabinets stand in flooded rows after three days of spring rain.
The night market sprawls through narrow alleys, generator lights swaying above tarps and wooden crates.
Snow settles on the abandoned grain elevator, its concrete silos gray against the winter morning.
The ferry terminal waits empty at noon, seagulls screaming over benches slick with recent rain.
In the monastery scriptorium, afternoon sun slants across oak tables scattered with parchment and ink.
The radio telescope array spreads across the desert basin, dishes turning slowly toward the evening sky.
At the border checkpoint, halogen lamps cast harsh shadows over the painted barrier and guard station.
The dance studio's mirrors reflect late morning light through windows fogged with yesterday's heat and breath.
In the coal mine's lamp room, dawn shift workers' helmets hang on numbered pegs along brick walls.
The rooftop garden blooms above the city, tomato plants heavy with fruit in the August twilight.
At the provincial archive, leather-bound registers line shelves reaching toward the vaulted ceiling in dim light.
The fishing village clings to cliffs above a harbor where boats rock in the pre-storm afternoon.
In the genetics laboratory, centrifuges whir behind glass at four in the morning, the building otherwise dark.
The truck stop diner glows neon through highway rain, its parking lot a mirror of red and blue.
At the geothermal plant, steam rises from pipes crossing the lava field in the pale Arctic summer.
The opera house stands empty after rehearsal, work lights illuminating the stage's painted backdrop of mountains.
In the weapons depot, crates stenciled with codes fill the warehouse under a single caged bulb.
The olive grove sleeps in midday heat, cicadas shrilling from silver-green branches heavy with unpicked fruit.
At the immigration office, morning sun bleaches the waiting room's notices and peeling linoleum floor.
The canal lock drips and echoes in early evening, its gates closed against the rising water.
In the photography darkroom, red safelight reveals trays of chemicals and paper pinned to drying lines.
The village square empties after the wedding feast, paper lanterns swaying above scattered tables and chairs.
At the weather station, instruments tick and whir on the tundra as midnight sun circles the horizon.
The parking garage's top level offers a view of downtown at dawn, concrete still warm from yesterday.
In the distillery, copper stills gleam in the afternoon as steam condenses on stone walls.
The train depot's waiting room echoes with departure announcements at eleven on a Sunday night.
At the archaeological dig, tarps flap over gridded trenches in the hour before the summer storm.
The printing press falls silent at shift change, leaving ink-smell and newsprint rolls in the basement dark.
In the cooling tower's shadow, cattails grow thick around stagnant pools that reflect the orange sunset.
The laundromat's windows fog with dryer heat against the freezing rain of a March evening.
